title: An initial unused factor gives an extra degeneracy of the split coproduct bar
statement:
Let $O$ be a small set, let $F,A,V$ be small ordinary categories [def-nagata-category] with object set $O$, and let $v:A\to V$ be a functor equal to the identity on $O$. All functors below fix $O$. Write $D*E$ for the coproduct of $D,E$ in categories with object set $O$: arrows are composable words of arrows of the factors modulo the composition and identity relations within each factor. Let $A_i$ denote labelled copies of $A$. Define an augmented simplicial category by
$$R_n=F*A_0*\cdots*A_n*V\quad(n\geq0),\qquad R_{-1}=F*V.$$
For $n\geq1$, the face $d_i:R_n\to R_{n-1}$, $0\leq i<n$, folds $A_i,A_{i+1}$ by the identity of $A$ and reindexes later copies; $d_n$ sends $A_n$ into $V$ by $v$. The degeneracy $s_i:R_n\to R_{n+1}$ inserts an unused copy of $A$ immediately after $A_i$, sending an old copy $k$ to copy $k$ if $k\leq i$ and to copy $k+1$ otherwise. All these maps fix $F,V$. The augmentation $\varepsilon_n:R_n\to F*V$ fixes $F,V$ and sends every $A_i$ into $V$ by $v$. Simplicial and augmented simplicial objects have the functor and operator conventions of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $h_{-1}:F*V\to R_0$ be the coproduct inclusions, and let $h_n:R_n\to R_{n+1}$ insert an unused copy before $A_0$, send each old copy $A_k$ identically to copy $A_{k+1}$, and fix $F,V$. These functors satisfy
$$\varepsilon_0h_{-1}=1_{F*V},\quad d_0h_n=1_{R_n},\quad d_1h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon_0,$$
$$d_{i+1}h_{n+1}=h_nd_i\quad(0\leq i\leq n+1),\qquad s_{i+1}h_n=h_{n+1}s_i\quad(0\leq i\leq n).$$
Consequently, for every $x,y\in O$, restricting these functors to the mapping sets gives an extra degeneracy in exactly the sense of [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction] for the augmentation of simplicial sets $R_\bullet(x,y)\to\operatorname{const}((F*V)(x,y))$. No freeness hypothesis on $F,A,V$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the word-quotient construction in the statement. A family of functors from its factors into a category on $O$, all fixing $O$, sends a composable word to the composite of its letter images. A relation composing two letters from the same factor is preserved because the corresponding factor map is a functor; an identity relation is preserved for the same reason. Thus the map descends to the quotient and preserves identities and composition [def-nagata-category]. It is unique because every arrow is a word in factor arrows. In particular two such functors are equal if their restrictions to every factor agree. The quotient is small: finite composable words in the small sets of factor arrows form a set, as does their quotient. These observations require neither free factors nor a unique reduced-word expression.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, proof, printed p.279: agent expansion of the split ordinary coproduct bar; the source leaves the contraction implicit.

proof.text: Construct all simplicial operators at once, using the contravariant convention of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For an order-preserving map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ and $0\leq k\leq n$, put $t_\alpha(k)=\min\{j\in[m]:k\leq\alpha(j)\}$, or $\infty$ if this set is empty. Define $T_\alpha:R_n\to R_m$ to fix $F,V$ and to send $A_k$ identically into $A_{t_\alpha(k)}$ when finite, and into $V$ by $v$ otherwise. Step 1 makes this a functor. For $\beta:[l]\to[m]$, extend $t_\beta(\infty)=\infty$. If $t_\alpha(k)=r<\infty$, monotonicity gives $k\leq\alpha(\beta(j))$ exactly when $r\leq\beta(j)$; if $t_\alpha(k)=\infty$, neither condition can hold. Taking the least such $j$ gives $t_{\alpha\beta}(k)=t_\beta(t_\alpha(k))$. Therefore $T_\beta T_\alpha=T_{\alpha\beta}$ on each $A_k$: either both preserve its arrow and reach the same labelled copy, or both apply $v$ once and reach $V$. They also agree on $F,V$. The identity ordinal map has $t(k)=k$, so $T_1=1$. These are the functor laws, without invoking a separate presentation theorem for the simplex category.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, proof, printed p.279: agent expansion of the split ordinary coproduct bar; the source leaves the contraction implicit.

proof.text: Identify the operators of step 2. For the injection $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ omitting $i<n$, the values of $t_{\delta_i}(k)$ are $k$ for $k<i$, $i$ for $k=i,i+1$, and $k-1$ for $k>i+1$. For $i=n$ they are $k$ for $k<n$ and $\infty$ for $k=n$. Thus $T_{\delta_i}$ is exactly the stated $d_i$. For the surjection $\sigma_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ repeating $i$, the values are $k$ for $k\leq i$ and $k+1$ for $k>i$, giving exactly $s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Each composite $\varepsilon_mT_\alpha$ fixes $F,V$ and sends each $A_k$ into $V$ by $v$, whether or not $T_\alpha$ has already sent it there. Hence $\varepsilon_mT_\alpha=\varepsilon_n$ by step 1. This proves that the prescribed operators give a simplicial category and that the displayed augmentations are natural to the constant category $F*V$.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, proof, printed p.279: agent expansion of the split ordinary coproduct bar; the source leaves the contraction implicit.

proof.text: The maps $h_{-1}$ and $h_n$ are functors by step 1: their restrictions are the inclusions of $F,V$, and for $h_n$ the identity functor from each old $A_k$ into $A_{k+1}$. The composite $\varepsilon_0h_{-1}$ fixes both factors of $F*V$, so it is the identity. For $d_0h_n$, each old $A_0$ first reaches $A_1$ and then the fold reaches $A_0$; an old $A_k$ with $k>0$ first reaches $A_{k+1}$ and is then reindexed back to $A_k$. Both functors fix $F,V$, so $d_0h_n=1$. Finally $h_0$ sends the sole old $A_0$ into $A_1$ of $R_1$, and $d_1$ then applies $v$ into $V$. This agrees with $h_{-1}\varepsilon_0$ on $A_0$ and on $F,V$, proving $d_1h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon_0$.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, proof, printed p.279: agent expansion of the split ordinary coproduct bar; the source leaves the contraction implicit.

proof.text: Check $d_{i+1}h_{n+1}=h_nd_i$ on $R_{n+1}$. Both sides fix $F,V$. If $0\leq i\leq n$, each side sends an old $A_k$ identically to $A_{k+1}$ for $k<i$, to $A_{i+1}$ for $k=i$ or $k=i+1$, and to $A_k$ for $k>i+1$: on the left shift first and fold at $i+1$; on the right fold at $i$ and shift. For the remaining index $i=n+1$, the left shifts $A_{n+1}$ to the last factor $A_{n+2}$ and then applies $v$, whereas the right applies $v$ immediately and then fixes $V$. Every $A_k$ with $k\leq n$ reaches $A_{k+1}$ on both sides. Step 1 now proves the functor equality in all the required indices, including this last-face case.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, proof, printed p.279: agent expansion of the split ordinary coproduct bar; the source leaves the contraction implicit.

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq n$, both $s_{i+1}h_n$ and $h_{n+1}s_i$ fix $F,V$ and send an old $A_k$ identically to $A_{k+1}$ when $k\leq i$ and to $A_{k+2}$ when $k>i$. Indeed on the left $k$ first becomes $k+1$, and insertion after position $i+1$ shifts it again precisely when $k>i$; on the right insertion after $i$ shifts precisely those same $k$, followed by the initial shift. Equality on factors gives $s_{i+1}h_n=h_{n+1}s_i$ by step 1.

source.place: Proposition 8.2, proof, printed p.279: agent expansion of the split ordinary coproduct bar; the source leaves the contraction implicit.

proof.text: Fix $x,y\in O$. Every functor constructed above fixes objects, so it restricts to a function on the indicated hom-sets. Restriction preserves identities and compositions of these functors, hence step 2 gives a simplicial set $X_n=R_n(x,y)$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and step 3 gives its augmentation to the constant set $S=(F*V)(x,y)$. The restricted $h_{-1},h_n$ satisfy all five displayed families of equations by steps 4--6. These are exactly the hypotheses called extra-degeneracy data in [lem-coef-extra-degeneracy-contraction], so they give the asserted extra degeneracy. Only this node's stated criterion is needed here; no homotopy-equivalence or Kan theorem is being used. Empty hom-sets are allowed throughout.
